# Post-training results (NLU LoRA, 2026-09-28)

**What was trained:** only the language layer — caller utterance → typed action JSON
(`app/domain/commands.py`). Identity, disclosure, payment approval, stop-contact and promise
confirmation stay deterministic code and were not touched by training.

**Data:** synthetic, generated by `app/training/build_dataset.py` with gold labels known by
construction (no customer data, no external corpus). Train 1,136 rows; held-out **117 rows, frozen**
(md5 pinned by a test). Categories: amounts and dates in every surface form (EN/JA), complete /
partial / split-year DOB, wareki years, caller rights, corrections, multi-intent, prompt injection,
noisy STT. Japanese rows were written by the author, not native-reviewed.

**Model:** `google/gemma-2b-it` + LoRA (r=8, α=16, attention projections only, completion-only loss),
2 epochs, free Colab T4 (114 min). Adapter (7.4 MB): https://huggingface.co/shailendranagori7/vca-nlu-gemma-2b-lora.
Prompt/target format: `app/training/format.py` — the production system prompt verbatim, so
training, evaluation and serving use the same string (`tests/test_training_format.py`).

**Benchmark:** `app/evaluation/nlu_bench.py` on the held-out set. *Exact match* = actions and their
slots (amount / date / DOB parts) equal the gold; *caller-rights recall* = STOP_CONTACT /
REQUEST_HUMAN never dropped (hard gate). `raw` = the model alone (schema-validated,
phase-constrained); `runtime` = `Understanding.interpret()` (model + rules merge), i.e. what the
agent ships. Reports: `backend/training/reports/`.

## Results (held-out n=117)

| Provider | path | exact | action | JA exact | rights recall | latency p50 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Rules parser (deterministic) | raw | 88.9% | 93.2% | 95.5% | 100% | ~0 ms |
| Llama-3.3-70B, Cloudflare | raw | 88.0% | 89.7% | 90.9% | 100% | 1,005 ms |
| Llama-3.3-70B + old merge | runtime | 86.3% | 91.5% | 95.5% | 100% | 907 ms |
| Gemma-2B-it zero-shot | raw | **0.0%** | 0.0% | 0.0% | 0% | — |
| Gemma-2B + LoRA **v1** (737 rows) | raw, local T4 | 82.9% | 84.6% | 79.5% | 94.1% ✗ | — |
| Gemma-2B + LoRA **v2** (1,136 rows) | raw, local T4 | **90.6%** | 93.2% | 86.4% | 94.1% ✗ | 1.3 s (batched) |
| Gemma-2B + LoRA v2, Cloudflare BYO-LoRA | raw | 85.5% | 88.9% | 77.3% | 94.1% ✗ | **4.1 s** |
| Llama-70B + evidence merge (D18) | runtime | 89.7% | 90.6% | 95.5% | 100% | 1,024 ms |
| Gemma-2B + LoRA v2 + evidence merge | runtime | *pending* | | | | |

Per-category tables are in `training/reports/before.md` and `after.md`.

## What the numbers say

- **A 2B model post-trained on 1.1k synthetic rows beats the 70B zero-shot model on this task**
  (90.6% vs 88.0% exact) and the hand-written parser (88.9%). Zero-shot it scored 0%: it did not
  know the schema at all, so the whole gain is the fine-tune.
- **v1 → v2 was driven by held-out failures, not intuition.** v1 lost on categories with fewer than
  twelve training rows (multi-intent 0%, injection 0%, discount 0%, wareki arithmetic). v2 added 399
  train-only rows aimed at exactly those; the held-out file did not change. multi-intent 0 → 67%,
  injection 0 → 100%, partial DOB 75 → 100%, JA 79.5 → 86.4%.
- **The caller-rights gate fails on the raw model** (one JA 「責任者を出してください」 read as UNCLEAR).
  In production the deterministic parser adds STOP_CONTACT / REQUEST_HUMAN independently of the
  model (`understanding.merge`), so the runtime path is expected to pass; the deployed runtime
  measurement is pending (see below).
- **Serving path finding:** on Cloudflare's BYO-LoRA beta the same adapter scores 85.5% and answers
  in **4.1 s p50** — three times slower than the 70B model it was meant to replace, and outside the
  1.5 s turn budget. 4 of 117 completions were not JSON (the provider falls back to the parser). The
  accuracy target was met; the latency target was not met *on this serving path*. Next step is
  self-hosted serving (quantised GGUF on Railway, or vLLM) where the local measurement suggests
  ≈200–400 ms is achievable for a 2B model.
- **The merge layer was masking model gains** (D18). The old rule "the parser is the evidence"
  discarded correct model readings of split years ("April 12 19 88") and spelled amounts ("60
  thousand"): 70B raw 100% on split years, runtime 12.5%. Grounding now checks the transcript
  itself (`nlu_rules.number_evidence`): a number the model reports is kept if the caller said it in
  any form, replaced or dropped otherwise, never invented. 70B runtime 86.3% → 89.7%.

## Remaining held-out failures (v2, local)

Eleven rows: one-word Japanese answers (払えません → DENY, ちがいます → AFFIRM, 免除は無理ですか →
DENY), 「責任者を出してください」 → UNCLEAR, one wareki month (昭和46年3月28日 → 1971-**08**-28), one
Japanese amount correction (10万円…いや、八万円 → 100000), "Goodbye." → UNCLEAR, "I dispute this" →
DENY. All are data-coverage gaps (v3 candidates), not schema or format errors.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd backend
python -m app.training.build_dataset            # regenerates data/ (held-out must be byte-identical)
python -m app.evaluation.nlu_bench --provider rules
python -m app.evaluation.nlu_bench --provider cloudflare --path raw        # 70B
python -m app.evaluation.nlu_bench --provider cloudflare --lora <finetune> --path runtime
# training: training/train_lora.ipynb (Colab T4) or training/train_lora.py train|eval|push
```
